$comment: The navigator's Small worlds section (src/ui/explore/worlds-panel.ts) and About a world (src/ui/explore/about.ts): loaded with their chunks.
ui.universe.worlds.loading: The small worlds are on their way…
ui.universe.worlds.intro: {asteroids, plural, =0 {No asteroids drawn} one {# asteroid drawn} other {# asteroids drawn}}, the largest first, of {loaded, plural, one {# loaded} other {# loaded}} from JPL’s Small-Body Database, each on its own orbit; {comets, plural, =0 {no comets near the Sun} one {# periodic comet within 8 au of the Sun} other {# periodic comets within 8 au of the Sun}}{tails, plural, =0 {} one {, # with tails} other {, # with tails}}.
ui.universe.worlds.none: No world by that name here.
ui.universe.worlds.more: {count, plural, one {# more: type to narrow} other {# more: type to narrow}}
ui.universe.worlds.note: Places from orbital elements: the Small-Body Database’s for the asteroids and comets (two-body orbits, drifting from the real ones over this decade by a tenth of a degree or so, up to two degrees for the Hildas, held in step with Jupiter, and more for comets), JPL’s mean elements fitted to Horizons for the moons. The asteroids’ light is enhanced in wide views so the belt shows; their places are not. The groups’ colours are illustrative. Arranged by orbit size, each asteroid is drawn in the planets’ plane at its orbit’s mean distance from the Sun, a diagram: the empty rings are the Kirkwood gaps, where Jupiter’s pull has cleared the orbits.
ui.universe.worlds.about.plain: {body}: {kind, select, asteroid {an asteroid} dwarf {a dwarf planet} comet {a comet} other {a moon of {host}}}.
ui.universe.worlds.about.axes: {a} by {b} by {c} across its axes (an ellipsoid)
ui.universe.worlds.about.fromH: {radius} in radius, estimated from its brightness
ui.universe.worlds.about.sphere: {radius} in mean radius; its shape not measured, it is drawn as a sphere
ui.universe.worlds.about.albedoValue: {value} of the light reaching it (geometric albedo)
ui.universe.worlds.about.albedoUnknown: not measured (drawn at a typical value)
ui.universe.worlds.about.surface: Its surface is drawn plain: no map of it is shown.
ui.universe.worlds.about.unimaged: About {percent}% of it was never imaged: drawn as a grey grid, not a guess.
ui.universe.worlds.about.sources: Sources: NASA JPL’s Small-Body Database and satellite tables (elements, sizes, spins), JPL Horizons, NSSDCA’s fact sheets (moons’ albedos and shapes), and the papers that measured the large trans-Neptunian objects.
